messages:
marta: quick heads-upwe've got RLS falling back to cheaper variants in the canary. question: do we keep full req/resp captures for those, or just minimal meters? i'm worried about billing accuracy + PII flow to cheaper audit buckets :grimacing:
simon: pipeline today is basically: ingress-meter -> routing -> sampling -> redact -> long-term-store. counters are accounted at ingress so quotas/billing are fine, but sampled artifacts include route and model info which means cheap-variant output can end up in audit if sampled enough.
tay: agree. i'd rather move to a two-stream model: always emit a tiny ingress-meter (non-sensitive) for quota/billing, keep routing decision in ephemeral debug if needed, and only write full payload to long-term audit when sampled AND redacted. that reduces PII surface on cheap variants.
marta: that sounds sensible. are there consequences for debugging rollouts if we don't persist route decision with every request?
simon: we can keep a short-lived route-trace store (TTL 1h) that records route decisions + light metadata to help canary debugging without long-term PII exposure. the long-term capture remains sampled+redacted.
tay: embedding edge-case: embeddings are "non-reversible-ish" but still sensitive. ops asked if we can store hashed provenance instead of raw vectors by default. my proposal: store only embedding_hash + meta unless tenant opts in. raw vector storage requires explicit opt-in, per-tenant KMS-protected bucket, and 30-day max retention.
simon: ingress-meter minimal schema (proposal):
```
ingress-meter.v1:
- tenant_id: t-12345
- req_ts: 2024-07-15T12:34:56Z
- token_count: 124
- route_hint: embeddings.lowcost.v2
- capture_flag: false  # only for bookkeeping, not PII
```
this event is JSON but kept tiny and logged to the metrics pipeline not object storage.
legal-bot: note: GDPR/DSAR implications: hashed embedding provenance might still be "personal data" depending on salt management. make sure per-tenant salts are handled and deletion flows remove both raw + hashed indexes. document retention semantics.
marta: console UX: when user toggles "enable full-capture" for a route, we should show an immediate cost estimate (projected GB/month based on recent qps), require manager confirmation for >X qps, and stage the toggle to edge proxies with a 3-min cooldown to avoid sudden floods. also display a live throttle indicator while the staged rollout is propagating.
tay: add a soft-cap: default max full-capture events per tenant per hour = 1k. if exceeded, throttle subsequent captures and emit an alert to tenant owner + support. allow overrides via support workflow.
simon: telemetry/dashboard additions:
- ingress-meter vs captured-logs counters per-route
- sampling ratio and effective token capture rate
- sampling bias heatmap (which tenants/routes are being captured more)
- redaction failure rate and PII detection counts (pre/post redact)
- storage projection widget (est. monthly cost for toggles)
marta: rollout plan idea: canary 5% tenants for 24h, collect metrics (sampled_rate, redaction_failures, storage_delta), then 25% for 48h, then full. include an automatic rollback if redaction-failure > 0.5% or storage overshoot >20% vs estimate.
ops-bot: [deploy-bot] ingress-meter + route-trace staging rollout started at 3239001140 :rocket:
simon: action: i'll write RFC for ingress-meter schema, retention, and where counters feed for billing. tay: i'll write RFC for embedding-hash-only default + opt-in raw vector storage. legal-bot: please produce DSAR/deletion guidance text for the RFCs. ux: wire the cost modal mockups and staged toggle flows.
marta: agreed. decision summary: two-stream model (tiny ingress-meter for billing/quotas + sampled+redacted full-capture for audit), short-lived route-trace for debugging, embeddings default to hash-only in audit buckets, console toggles require cost modal + staged propagation + per-tenant gating, and soft-cap throttles on full-capture. tagging resolved unless anyone objects. :white_check_mark:
